subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw add manifest-declared install-time config intent for third-party plugins, and what path limits, confirmation, conflict/array behavior, provenance, and uninstall guidance must it require?
rationale: This changes plugin installation from enabling package metadata to allowing package metadata to mutate persisted user configuration, which crosses product, upgrade-safety, and security boundaries that source inspection cannot decide.

options.title: Define Guarded Config Intent
options.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

options.title: Keep Manual Setup For Now
options.body: Reject manifest-driven writes and keep plugins using docs, setup flows, provider auth, or explicit `openclaw config patch` until a safer contract is designed.

options.title: Tie It To Trust Metadata
options.body: Require ClawHub or package trust metadata before a plugin can request install-time config mutation.

recommendation.title: Define Guarded Config Intent
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as product/security follow-up and have recent manifest/install documentation history.
